Our invoice previews have two billing discrepancies. A USD line for 105 cents
with 10% tax in line-tax mode currently returns 11 cents tax / 116 cents total;
it should return 10 / 115. Another 105-cent line with discounts of 50%, then
10 cents off, and 10% tax returns 47 cents net / 5 cents tax / 52 cents total;
it should return 43 / 4 / 47. The second discrepancy is not just a final-total
rounding issue.

Investigate and repair the pricing library behind `src/index.js`'s CommonJS
named export `buildInvoice`. Keep its existing API and the full contract in the
source JSDoc, including ordered discounts, exact integer-cent arithmetic,
half-even rounding, credits, allocation, both tax modes, and input validation.
Preserve behavior outside the reported cases. Do not add dependencies.

Work only in the current directory. Do not modify `test/` or `package.json`.
Verify the fix with `node --test`.

content.text:
I fixed both discrepancies; they came from two separate bugs, one per file. `node --test` passes both tests (2/2), and the reported cases now give 10/115 and 43/4/47.

**1. Rounding (`src/rounding.js`, `roundRatio`).** It used `Math.round(Number(n) / Number(d))`. That rounds exact halves up, so 10.5 became 11, and it loses precision once numbers pass 2^53. It now uses whole-number (BigInt) division: it splits the value into a whole part and a remainder, then rounds by comparing twice the remainder with the divisor. An exact half goes to the even number. The result is still checked with `cents`, so a value too large for a JavaScript number still throws `RangeError`. This one function handles rounding for both percent discounts and tax, so this change fixes the first case.

**2. Discount order (`src/discounts.js`, `applyDiscounts`).** It re-sorted every discount list so fixed discounts ran before percent ones, which ignores the order you supply. Your second case therefore ran as 105 − 10 = 95, then 50% of 95 = 47.5. Old rounding made that 48 off, leaving 47 net and 5 tax. I removed the sort, so discounts apply in the order given: 105 − 52 (52.5 rounded to even) = 53, then 53 − 10 = 43, then tax on 43 at 10% = 4.3, rounded to 4. That's why this wasn't just a final-total rounding issue. The sort fed the half-even rounding problem. The same function also handles invoice-level discounts, so their order is fixed too.

A quick script also confirmed that halves round to even for both signs (0.5 → 0, 1.5 → 2, −1.5 → −2) and that a result rounding to −0 comes back as 0. It also confirmed that an exact value just above 2^53 rounds correctly and an out-of-range result throws `RangeError`.

I also read through credits, allocation, both tax modes and input validation against the JSDoc and found no other mismatches. Nothing else changed, and I added no dependencies.

**Behaviour change:** every percent discount and tax calculation that lands on exactly half a cent now rounds to even instead of up. Invoices with several discounts whose list doesn't put fixed amounts first will also come out differently. Both changes follow the documented rules, but existing previews in those cases will show different amounts.
